title: fix(app-shell): pending changes folds platform-written system fields and derived keys into one collapsed line
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9CEUVquf4gyNp5rXBUzghZZ)_

Fixes #25890

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

Studio's pending-changes drill-in (`DraftChangesPanel`) listed a new object's platform-injected system columns (`created_at`, `created_by`, `owner_id`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`) as fields the author added, and its derived `nameField` under "Also changed", next to the one field the author actually typed. Following the triage ruling ("Pending changes lists what the author changed. Platform-provisioned system fields and derived keys belong in a collapsed 'generated' group, not in the author's diff."):

- **System fields fold.** In `computeChangeDetail`, a field this publish adds or removes, where every definition the two bodies carry has `system: true`, moves to a new `generated` list. `system: true` is the spec's own mark (`FieldSchema.system`: "Auto-injected system/audit field … Tools that surface system fields separately from author-declared business fields should branch on this flag"). No name list is kept in the panel. The read localises the injected columns' labels, so byte-identity against `injectedSystemColumnDefs` cannot answer this on a served body; the mark can.
- **Derived keys fold.** A top-level `nameField` goes to `generated` when its value equals the `@objectstack/spec/data` `provisionPrimary` derivation over the body without the pointer. That is the same test the registry's write-side strip (`stripProvisionedPrimaryFrom`) uses. A pointer naming a field the derivation would not pick is the author's choice and stays an author row.
- **What stays an author row.** A system field whose definition *differs* between the published and draft bodies (for example, the author relabelled `owner_id`) stays an author row: the platform injects the same definition on both reads, so a difference is an edit. The objectui#13125 rule (`system` AND `hidden`, e.g. `__search`) still drops those rows outright, unchanged.
- **The fold renders as one collapsed line**, "Generated by the platform (N)" (「平台生成（N）」), with a toggle that shows those rows. It stays collapsed in the confirm posture too.
- **A new item's keys are headed "Includes:"** (「包含：」) instead of "Also changed:" (「其他变更：」). Every key of an item that does not exist yet is part of it, not some other change.
- Two new i18n keys (`preview.changes.detailNewKeys`, `preview.changes.generatedGroup`) are added to all ten packs, because the key-parity test requires every pack.
- `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json`: the registry-source hash is re-recorded by `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs`. The manifest bytes did not change (sha256 `1f6e1ccb925a…`, 106 components).

The card's repro (new object 「报修工单」, OWD private) now expands to `+ 名称 name`, then `Includes: + label + name + sharingModel`, then one collapsed `Generated by the platform (6)` line (the five system columns plus `nameField`).

## Acceptance notes

- **Deviation from the dispatch's acceptance wording ("only the authored field(s) plus one folded system-fields line").** The new object's authored top-level keys `label`, `name` and `sharingModel` are still listed, under "Includes:". The ruling folds *platform-provisioned* fields and *derived* keys, and those three are authored in the create dialog. A first cut dropped `name`/`label` for new items (the row already shows them), but that reversed seven existing pins in four files (`DraftChangesPanel.test.tsx` "classifies a NEW item", `noChangeAndKeySplit-11807`, `posture-12517`, `protectionEnvelope-12594`), which the dispatch asked to keep green. So it was reverted. If the maintainer wants a new item's name/label hidden as well, that is a follow-up with those pins rewritten deliberately.
- **One existing pin updated on purpose.** In `DraftChangesPanel.fieldRows-13125.test.tsx`, `owner_id` and `created_at` were "listed" controls ("this card does not widen the rule"). They now assert placement in the generated group, and that the drop rule still leaves them in the detail behind the toggle.
- The panel only sees served bodies, so an author who declares a column that the platform also injects, with `system: true` on it, reads as platform-written when added. That is the spec's stated meaning of the mark.

## Tests

At head `f96a8519`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/i18n/ packages/app-shell/src/preview/` (from `ui/`): **Test Files 120 passed (120), Tests 1585 passed | 13 skipped**.
- New `DraftChangesPanel.generatedGroup-25890.test.tsx` (9 tests). It pins the card's repro using the spec's real `injectedSystemColumnDefs` with zh-localised labels, plus four controls: a system field the author changed, an author-chosen `nameField`, a system field added on an update, and an audit-shaped field without the mark.
- **Ablation, once.** I disabled the fold predicate through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `6c92a1c5…` to `805a4a90…`). The new suite went **4 failed | 5 passed**. The file was restored to its HEAD blob `6c92a1c5…`. The suite resolves `DraftChangesPanel` from source through the ui vitest alias, so no dist rebuild was involved.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json`): **Done / Done**.
- `node scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` (ui): exit 0. eslint on the touched files: 0 errors. The 6 warnings are all in code this PR does not change.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `f96a8519` derived 46 families. All 46 ran with exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: "46 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 46 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)". At the earlier head `6577bce6`, `check-sdui-manifest` was red because the ui source hash had moved. The regeneration commit fixed it, and the check is green at `f96a8519`. CI families are left to the PR's check-runs.

Out of bounds and untouched: `ui/.github/**` and the root `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
